races.name: Supporting Ayr Racecourse, The John Cocking Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
25% Off Lunch At Western House Hotel Handicap

runners_data.name: King's Crown
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with headgear (tongue-tie/hood) who has failed to win or place on good going in two recent attempts at 5f; trainer Dods has modest 14-day form and the sim-going record here is poor (2/15), making this a difficult profile to fancy from the rear in a race likely dominated up front.
runners_data.comment: Improved recently, finishing 3rd two starts back and 4th last time, with proven form over today's distance and going and a fair break since running; still without a win in his last six starts but on a better run of late.

runners_data.name: Curious Rover
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose 11 runs on similar going include one win and three placings at 5f — the best good-going record of the closers in this field — and Jason Hart's retention gives some confidence this can hit the frame if a pace wobble develops late.
runners_data.comment: Boasts the strongest form of this field, with three 4ths in his last five starts and proven distance/going form; the danger is fitness after a 38-day break, but on that level of consistency he's hard to overlook.

runners_data.name: Brazen Idol
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse returning quickly (11 days) for John Ryan; posted two second-place finishes over 6f which suggests the drop to 5f here may stretch the frame too far, and the sim-going record of 4/15 is modest, though good-going form is not a concern.
runners_data.comment: Freshest of these on an 11-day turnaround, with two runner-up efforts among his last five starts hinting at latent ability over today's distance and going; the concern is that his latest start was an 8th, so consistency remains the query.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and sole pace-setter, Paul Mulrennan takes over for Jim Goldie who is in strong 14-day form (4/34); excellent five-race record on good going at 5f (5W8P in 13 runs) is the standout stat, though a second run in eight days is a small watch point on fitness.
runners_data.comment: Mare returning quickly just 8 days after finishing 2nd last time out, with a win earlier in her last six starts showing latent ability but three finishes outside the frame in that spell too; proven form over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Lion's House
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse whose actual tendency to finish at the rear is noted — the sim-going record on good is very thin (2/15) and 0W0P in those runs; Connor Beasley cannot conjure a lead position that does not suit this horse's style, so the redistribution to midfield flatters its likely real-race positioning.
runners_data.comment: Fitful form so far, with a 2nd four starts back the highlight among mostly modest finishes; 23 days off and a moderate official mark raise questions, but the placed form over today's distance and going marks him a threat.

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist by trade despite wearing a hood (p), Ewan Whillans's runner won once at 5f on good ground but the form string 508671 shows high variance; redistribution means William Pyle will likely find the horse further back than the midfield tag implies, and the recent 18-day freshen-up offers some hope.
runners_data.comment: Struck form with a win last time out following a string of modest efforts in the runs before; quick to return within 18 days, and with proven distance/going form, the query is whether that upturn holds.

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip on good going and placed again in follow-up, giving Barry McHugh genuine course-and-distance credentials; a natural hold-up horse who will be asked to find ground on a front-runner not under pressure, which tempers the appeal despite the solid recent form.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back and confirmed that form with a 3rd next time, but disappointing with a 7th last time out; a 33-day layoff adds a fitness question, though proven form over today's distance and going keeps him competitive.

runners_data.name: Thistle Nil
runners_data.note: Only four career runs with thin good-ground data (2/4), and a hold-up style means Rhys Elliott (claiming 5lb) faces the task of closing from the rear on a horse settling into a sustained gallop — the 9-furlong outing in the form string (9th) also raises a slight stamina-in-reverse query over 5f.
runners_data.comment: Form figures are wildly inconsistent — a win two starts back sandwiched between two finishes well off the pace, and an 8th last time out; quick enough back within 9 days, but on balance he rates a rank outsider here.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old with multiple 5f runs on good going but still without a win in 15 similar-going starts; Shane Gray must find ground on Woohoo from a rear position in a race that provides minimal pace pressure — fine each-way profile at best given age and recent 637 form.
runners_data.comment: A 3rd two starts back stands out among mixed form figures, with a below-par 7th last time out the low point; quick to return within 8 days, and with proven distance/going form, there's enough here to suggest more than the latest finish implies.

runners_data.name: Falcon Queen
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old filly against older horses, racing with headgear (h) and carrying only 125lbs; only 1 from 5 runs on good going and 0 wins across the board, and as a hold-up type on a track where the front-runner is uncontested, David Allan will have work to do — the youth and potential angle is the only positive.
runners_data.comment: Three each-way efforts (all 4th) preceded a below-par 8th and 9th in her last two starts, a decline that's hard to ignore; she has raced over today's distance before, but a 23-day break and that faded form make her tough to fancy without stronger claims.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: The second prominent-style horse in the race and the one most likely to track Woohoo through the race; Jim Goldie's yard is flying (6/53 in 14 days) and Lauren Young's 5lb claim is a live weight-carrying advantage — good-going form at 5f is strong (8/15 runs, 1W5P) and a close pitch to the front-runner gives her the best late-closing opportunity in the field.
runners_data.comment: Consistently competitive, with three placed efforts in her last six starts including a win four starts back, though only 4th last time out; back within 13 days and with proven distance/going form, but she'll need more than that to trouble the principals.

races.paceDynamic: Woohoo is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 5f handicap and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival pressing from the gates — Wee Mary is the only other prominent-style horse in the field, meaning Woohoo can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on good ground without being harried into an unsustainable early tempo. The bulk of the field — Lion's House, Jm Jhingree, Hi Lord, Thistle Nil, Our Absent Friends and Falcon Queen — are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there are more closers than the rear can accommodate; they will not all get as far back as they want, and the ones who do face the challenge of making up ground on a horse that has not been pressed early. Wee Mary, showing excellent recent form on good ground with multiple top-two finishes over this course and distance, is best placed to track Woohoo and mount a prominent challenge. This race shape — a steady-to-fair pace set by a single front-runner on a flat, fair-ground track — strongly favours horses racing prominently or tracking close to the pace, as late closers will be asked to find too much ground against a front-runner that has not been softened up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Woohoo Controls, Wee Mary Chases
scenarios.trigger: If Woohoo gets a clean break and Wee Mary tracks closely, setting up a true pace-vs-pace duel in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Woohoo controls from flag to finish at a fair gallop, with Wee Mary the only horse close enough to seriously threaten entering the final furlong; the pair draw clear of the hold-up horses who cannot reel in a front-runner who has been given a soft lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Woohoo's recent eight-day turnaround catches up with her late and she ties up inside the final furlong, giving closers a chance.
scenarios.body: A moderate early pace paradoxically keeps hold-up horses too far back to land a telling blow, but a genuine late fade from Woohoo opens a narrow window for the best of the closers; Curious Rover's strong recent form on good ground and Hi Lord's course-and-distance win make them the most credible beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Wee Mary pushes Woohoo harder than expected from the break, lifting the tempo and creating a truly run race that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: A contested pace drains front-runner reserves and the race becomes a flat-out sprint from the two-furlong pole; horses racing third or fourth — those redistributed hold-up types who land a middle position — can sustain a late run, with Curious Rover and Our Absent Friends best suited given their decent good-ground profiles at 5f.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Lands In Right Spot
scenarios.trigger: If the draw or early traffic shuffles the field unusually and a hold-up type secures an unplanned prominent pitch close to the pace.
scenarios.body: An atypical race shape sees one of the redistributed closers accidentally tracking Woohoo early, converting their natural ability into a race-winning position; Hi Lord, who has won on good going at this trip, and Jm Jhingree, who has won at 5f on good ground, are the most likely to capitalise if fortune places them in the right spot.

watchPoints.text: Wee Mary needs to secure second spot behind Woohoo from the gates — if she gets hampered at the start or is shuffled back, the race shape dramatically reduces her chance of landing a blow.

Woohoo's eight-day turnaround for Jim Goldie deserves monitoring in the closing stages; if she shows any sign of tying up inside the final furlong, the hold-up horses — particularly Curious Rover and Hi Lord — are closest in the market to benefit.

Several redistributed hold-up horses (Lion's House, Jm Jhingree, Hi Lord, Our Absent Friends, Falcon Queen) will likely jostle for midfield and rear positions early; congestion and traffic between the two-furlong pole and the furlong marker could compromise multiple closers simultaneously.

Thistle Nil's last run was over 9 furlongs (well out of trip), and the drop back to 5f with a 5lb claimer on board in what is essentially a sprint is an unknown — watch whether the horse jumps cleanly and holds a position or gets outpaced from the outset.

runners_data.name: Azuinthejungle
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has been competitive over 5f on Good ground but steps up to 6f here where her form is unproven — the extra furlong may suit or may stretch her, and Alex Jary's 3lb claim helps offset the weight; Tinkler's yard is not in red-hot form at 1/29 over 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: A third last time out headlines a workmanlike spell, and he's quickly back, just 17 days on, proven over today's distance and going already. Yet to get his head in front in that run and the yard is out of form, but he tops our figures.

runners_data.name: Taygar
runners_data.note: Consistently prominent and remarkably consistent in placing over this exact trip and going combination — 0 wins from 7 placed efforts at 6f on Good suggests she may find one too good again, but her profile fits this race shape as well as anyone's and Sean Kirrane rides without a claim at full weight.|
runners_data.comment: Three seconds in a row precede last time's fourth, with an eighth the outlier five starts back, and she's already proven over today's distance and going. Consistently knocking on the door without getting there, and the 27 days since her last start is the query.

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who will dictate the pace but is stepping out of her natural comfort zone over 6f after a run of 5f efforts — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 reflects that she is effectively asked to do a different job here, and Paul Mulrennan will need to judge the fractions carefully given her age (8) and recent busy schedule (8 days since last run).|
runners_data.comment: A win six starts back has been followed by modest finishes, though last time's third hints he's coming back to himself, and he's already proven over today's distance and going. Fresh from a run just eight days ago, with the moderate form in between the main knock.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Prominent-style filly with an exceptional placed record at this trip including two seconds over 6f on Good — the 39-day absence is worth noting but Goldie's yard has been active, and the combination of Lauren Young's 5lb claim and solid each-way form makes her interesting in a race she is well-suited by in style.|
runners_data.comment: Three straight seconds are the highlight of her recent form, though a seventh and ninth further back temper the read, and she already has today's distance and going covered. Over five weeks since that last run and yet to convert those places into a win.

runners_data.name: White Ladder
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has actually won over 6f on Good ground, which gives her a profile edge over the other closers — Sean Bowen takes the ride and the 7-day turnaround from her last run suggests she is fit and ready; her best chance comes if the pace develops into something faster than expected.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to cap a run of placed efforts - two thirds and a second before that - and he's quickly back, just seven days on, already proven over today's distance and going. He now rates well above his official mark, the chief question being whether the leap holds.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Kisses
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose recent form includes a poor run over 6f on Soft and a 14th over 6f — the switch back to Good ground is a positive given her best form figure came on Good, but the form string (3-4609) reads with some inconsistency and the race shape does not set up naturally for a closer from off the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Whiskey Kisses opened this run with a third but has tailed off badly since, down to a ninth last time out. Quickly back within seven days with distance and going proven, but the finishing positions need to turn around to be of real interest; still without a win of late.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: In-form on similar going with two wins and four places from 12 runs on Good or similar — a true hold-up horse whose instinct is to race from the rear, but the density of hold-up types in this field means he is unlikely to get the dream closing run he needs; the STYLE_FIT note reflects that his natural position is further back than the map shows, and his OR of 50 may underrate him on a good day.|
runners_data.comment: Royal Duke is winless in his last five, a lone third the only relief among finishes of sixth and seventh. Quickly back within a week with distance and going proven, but this looks a struggle near the foot of our figures.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has won over this course configuration, giving him a live place claim on form — a genuine closer by inclination whose chance depends on a pace that tests the prominent runners, but being mapped into midfield because of the hold-up congestion means Jake Dickson (7lb claim) will need to adapt his ride; the 18-day break appears manageable for Goldie.|
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back sits amid a mixed sequence that also features an eighth, though last time's third was a step forward. Back within three weeks and already suited by today's distance and going, but rated among the outsiders here.

runners_data.name: Wee Dresser
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old whose best form has come at 6f on Good ground with a third last time out on that surface — trained by Katie Scott whose 14-day strike rate is 0/16 and who carries bottom weight; likely to race from the hold-up position naturally but faces a stiff task against more experienced rivals if the pace doesn't truly collapse.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts, with a third three starts back the only bright spot among finishes no better than sixth elsewhere. Back within three weeks and already proven over today's distance and going, but sits bottom of our order for this race.

races.paceDynamic: Water Of Leith is the confirmed front-runner and will look to dictate from the front over this 6f at Ayr on Good ground, setting a sustainable rather than suicidal pace given there is no genuine rival pressing for the lead. Azuinthejungle and Taygar are both prominent types who will look to sit just behind or alongside Water Of Leith in the first two furlongs, meaning the early order is likely to be competitive without being truly scorching. Thunderstorm Katie is another horse likely to race prominently, adding further density to the front half of the field and compressing the pack. This shape — a controlled, even-tempo 6f with several horses racing close to the pace on Good ground — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs rather than true closers swooping from the rear; the hold-up brigade face an uphill task against this pace map. Note that Royal Duke and Doon The Glen are genuine hold-up types pushed into a midfield mapping because this field carries more rear-rankers than the race shape can comfortably accommodate — White Ladder and Wee Dresser are the horses most likely to actually secure a rearward position naturally.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith dictates an honest but unchallenged pace and the prominent stalkers travel within a length entering the final 2f
scenarios.body: Water Of Leith sets the tempo from flagfall and the prominent horses — Taygar and Azuinthejungle — track closely and are best placed to pounce as the field straightens; on Good ground at Ayr over 6f this shape rewards horses who travel smoothly and don't get shuffled back. Taygar's consistent placed form over exactly this trip and going makes her the textbook beneficiary, while Thunderstorm Katie's relentless second-place record at this distance gives her strong claims if she gets the prominent berth.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Front Runner Scores
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith is left completely uncontested and the pace is genuinely slow enough to allow her to coast and quicken
scenarios.body: With no horse pressing hard for the lead, Water Of Leith controls every fraction and conserves enough energy to repel the challengers in the final furlong; at 8 years old she is a veteran who knows her job and Jim Goldie's yard has been active. The prominent trackers would be playing catch-up against a horse who has dictated every yard, particularly if the pace is deceptively measured.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners burn each other out mid-race and the pace proves faster than anticipated, opening a gap for those coming from further back
scenarios.body: White Ladder is the most naturally talented of the closers, having won over exactly this trip and course configuration on Good ground, and could motor through if the front half collectively tie up. Wee Dresser has placed twice at this trip over Good going at 6f and could also grab a minor share, though the pace profile makes this scenario genuinely less likely given the controlled nature of Water Of Leith's expected lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Jostling For Position
scenarios.trigger: If the multiple prominent types clash sharply for early position and the tempo becomes ragged and contested
scenarios.body: Azuinthejungle, Taygar and Thunderstorm Katie all pressing for the same real estate could create early interference and a faster-than-expected opening 2f, leaving those who switch off early in the best shape. Royal Duke and Doon The Glen — both true hold-up types who have been pushed into a midfield mapping — would struggle to capitalise even in this scenario as they are not ideally positioned for it, but a late-running White Ladder could profit if the front group genuinely burns out.

watchPoints.text: Water Of Leith leads unchallenged — if Paul Mulrennan takes her to the front unchallenged and gets away with a very slow early pace, she could prove very hard to reel in given the hold-up horses are not ideally positioned to close.

Taygar's no-win streak — she has been placed seven times at this trip on Good going without winning; if she hits the front she may find one or more rivals going past her late, watch for a repeat of that pattern.

Prominent traffic danger in the first furlong — with Azuinthejungle, Taygar, Thunderstorm Katie and Water Of Leith all likely to race in the first three lengths, there is a meaningful risk of crowding and early interference that could unsettle any of them.

White Ladder hold-up position — Sean Bowen is a strong judge of pace and if he reads a genuinely contested early race he may be able to deliver White Ladder with a well-timed run; watch where she is after 2f to assess if the shape is opening up for closers.

Doon The Glen visor effect — the headgear and Jim Goldie's course knowledge are worth tracking in running; if Dickson can get him into a position slightly closer than his natural style over the first half, the visor could sharpen his finish on Good ground where he has form.

races.name: racingtv.com/freetrial Handicap

runners_data.name: Braes Of Doune
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed pace-setter; Jim Goldie's eight-year-old has strong place form on similar Good ground (2W8P in 15 sim-going runs) and at 8f Ayr specifically, and an uncontested lead is his absolute optimum — top weight of 127lbs is the primary concern, and his style fit in a lone-leader role here is near-perfect.
runners_data.comment: A 2nd three starts back is the standout in modest form otherwise, with a 6th last time out the most recent evidence; 24 days off and only fair figures make him tough to fancy, though proven distance/going form offers a sliver of hope.

runners_data.name: Millbuie
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' five-year-old returns quickly (8 days), wore a tongue-strap last time and finished third on Good ground recently, but his natural hold-up style means he is quietly tucked into midfield as one of several closers who cannot all get to the rear; a patient Pyle ride will be required.
runners_data.comment: Latest 3rd matched another 3rd three starts back, either side of modest efforts in between, so he's not without competitive form; quick to return within 8 days and with proven distance/going form, though the bare figures leave him with plenty to find here.

runners_data.name: Golden Valour
runners_data.note: A decade-old course veteran who has placed on Good ground before, but his preferred hold-up role is compromised by the overcrowded rear of this field — Fentiman will need to find a clean passage, and a record of just one win from 15 similar-going runs is sobering.
runners_data.comment: Nothing better than 5th across his last five starts, a run of finishes offering little encouragement on bare form; quick to return within 8 days and with proven distance/going form, but he otherwise rates the outsider of this field.

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Jason Hart takes the mount on Tristan Davidson's four-year-old, who carries a hefty 130lbs and has not won on Good ground in 15 attempts — a genuine come-from-behind type who needs stronger pace than Braes Of Doune is likely to set to make his late effort count.
runners_data.comment: A 3rd two starts back, and followed that with a fair 5th last time out; a 28-day absence since raises a fitness question, but proven distance/going form keeps him among the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Thats My Boy Luke
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old wears blinkers and has strong course-and-distance credentials (2W6P on sim-going in 13 runs at the trip), and David Allan knows this horse well; his natural style means he will sit mid-division here and he shapes as one of the likelier challengers if the leader weakens.
runners_data.comment: Modest but fairly consistent, with a 4th last time out matching his level after finishing outside the frame in three of his last five starts; 22 days since that run, and though distance/going form is proven, there's little here suggesting marked improvement.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Pete
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler has gone 0/23 in the past 14 days and this five-year-old has a bleak recent form string of 56-000 with 15th and 13th on softer ground; placed on Good before, but he is a true hold-up horse squeezed into midfield, and apprentice Alex Jary's 3lb claim is the only positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Bare form figures are unremarkable — three unplaced efforts in his last five starts — but a strong speed rating hints at more, and he has proven distance/going form; a trainer at 0% over the last fortnight and a 29-day absence are the concerns.

runners_data.name: Gressington
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's five-year-old wears a visor and has been running mainly over 6-7f — stepping back to a mile after a 13-day turnaround looks a stretch, and his form figures of 060807 at a shorter trip on Good ground offer little encouragement for a prominent draw here.
runners_data.comment: A modest sequence by bare results, with nothing better than 6th across his last six starts, though strong speed figures hint at more ability than the placings show; back within 13 days and with proven distance/going form, he's open to marked improvement.

runners_data.name: Eagles Dream
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson runs this four-year-old just nine days after its last run; the historical trip profile is striking — it has run over 9-14f — and dropping to a flat mile at Ayr is a significant distance question mark, even with nine of 11 runs on Good ground.
runners_data.comment: Modest on bare form — an 8th last time out followed a moderate spell — but she returns quickly within 9 days, owns proven distance/going form, and a standout speed figure points to more than the results show, making her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Starliner
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's five-year-old won over 8f on Good ground (1W2P from six similar-going runs) and Connor Beasley is an assured partner; wears a hood and has placed at this course before, making him one of the better-credentialed hold-up types in a field where that profile dominates.
runners_data.comment: Yo-yo form figures, with a win five starts back followed by an indifferent spell that includes back-to-back 8ths in his last two starts; a quick 7-day turnaround and proven distance/going form keep him in the shake-up, but he needs to rediscover that level again.

races.paceDynamic: Braes Of Doune is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of nine and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure him, he is expected to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo on Good ground over Ayr's flat mile. The eight horses behind him are overwhelmingly hold-up types by nature, meaning the pace will be honest but not frantically strong — Braes Of Doune sets his own rhythm and is unlikely to be chased down early. Runninsonofagun, Whiskey Pete, Thats My Boy Luke and others are genuine hold-up or come-from-behind horses who are mapped to midfield purely because the rear of the field is overcrowded with similar profiles; they cannot all get their preferred last-off-the-bridle position. This race shape — a single, uncontested leader dictating a measured gallop — strongly favours horses that can race prominently or mid-division with cover and produce a sustained, progressive run into the straight, rather than those who rely on a truly strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Braes Of Doune Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Braes Of Doune gets a clean lead and sets a comfortable, controlled tempo that he can sustain into the Ayr straight.
scenarios.body: He pings from the gates, establishes his rhythm unchallenged, and the hold-up horses behind him are left with insufficient pace to close off — his 2W8P record on similar going underlines this is his preferred scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mid-Division Improver Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace strings the field out in a line and a progressive mid-division horse threads through on the inside rail in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The contained tempo means gaps open later rather than closing early, rewarding any runner who has tracked the pace through the mid-section and possesses a reliable turn of foot on Good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Denied By Dawdle
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so steady that hold-up horses are left with too much ground to make up and run into traffic on the home turn.
scenarios.body: Those mapped furthest back — Gressington, Golden Valour, Whiskey Pete — lack the natural kick to bridge a conservative pace, and the redistribution of multiple hold-up types into midfield creates a bunched, slow-motion finish that favours whoever is handiest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Helps Front Two
scenarios.trigger: If Braes Of Doune is briefly pressed by a runner breaking prominence unexpectedly, only to find that pursuer fade, leaving him and a close-up companion to fill the frame.
scenarios.body: A brief mid-race injection of pressure paradoxically burns off the closers, and the two horses who have raced closest to Braes Of Doune throughout are best placed to pick up any pieces.

watchPoints.text: Braes Of Doune's ability to secure a clean, uncontested lead is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if anything forces him wider or challenges him through the first quarter-mile, the tempo and the entire race shape changes.

Starliner's headgear (hood) and Beasley's tactical nous make this horse one to monitor through the mid-race — if he travels smoothly just behind the lead group, he could be the prime beneficiary of a slowly-run contest.

Thats My Boy Luke carries 128lbs in blinkers and David Allan may try to push him into a closer position than his natural style suggests, especially given his strong sim-going record — watch for an early move to sit third or fourth.

Eagles Dream's distance profile (best form over 9-14f) makes the drop to a flat mile worth watching in running — if he fades in the final furlong having travelled well, it is a trip issue rather than a form collapse.

Gressington steps up markedly in trip from recent 6-7f starts and a visor is fitted — if he settles and stays on past beaten horses, note it as a potential trip discovery; if he fades before the distance, it confirms the step up is beyond him.

runners_data.name: Monhammer
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with solid placed form at 7f on good ground (2nd and 3rd in recent efforts at this trip), but a natural hold-up horse whose preferred ground at the rear of the field is compromised here by the sheer number of closers — he is likely to find himself racing in midfield rather than from his favoured position, which tempers his chance.|
runners_data.comment: A fair 3rd three starts back was followed by a closer 2nd, though he could only manage 4th last time out; quick to return within 8 days and with proven distance/going form, a placed finish looks the realistic ceiling here.

runners_data.name: Due Respect
runners_data.note: Four-year-old lightly raced for Gary Rutherford, returning after 21 days with modest recent figures (8th, 7th) but two placed efforts at 7f in good ground earlier in the form string; by inclination a hold-up horse, though with so many closers in this field he is unlikely to settle as deep as he ideally wants, making his finishing effort harder to execute.|
runners_data.comment: Her form has edged forward of late — 7th and 8th early in this run but a 4th last time out a step forward; 21 days off and modest speed figures leave her the outsider of this field, despite proven distance/going form.

runners_data.name: Bantz
runners_data.note: Disappointing recent figures (8th, 9th) mask what is a genuinely back-to-form type who prefers to come from off the pace at 7f; Sean Kirrane takes the ride after 27 days off, and while his deep closer's instinct is his strength, getting shuffled into the pack of redistributed hold-up horses in midfield could blunt what should be a clear run from the rear.|
runners_data.comment: A modest sequence throughout, with nothing better than 7th across his last five starts and a 9th his most recent effort; 27 days off compounds the concerns, though proven distance/going form is at least in his favour.

runners_data.name: Ramon Di Loria
runners_data.note: The key pace-setter in this race — an eight-year-old who has been placed in three of his last four 7f outings on good ground and has Greg Fairley, who knows this horse well, on board; trainer Ewan Whillans has a recent winner in the yard (1/8 T14), and with no rival likely to seriously contest the front, he has every chance to control the race from flag to finish.|
runners_data.comment: Metronomically consistent, with three 3rd-placed finishes in his last six starts including his latest run, plus a quick 8-day turnaround and proven distance/going form; the question is whether that consistency can translate into passing rivals rather than just matching them.

runners_data.name: Tap Dancer
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan's mount is a four-year-old with all his recent form at 10f-11f, and this drop to 7f is a significant and untested trip change — Jim Goldie's operation is firing (6/46 T14), and the shortening of the race could unlock latent speed, but the distance question mark is real and his hold-up style at a reduced trip on a flat track is an unresolved puzzle.|
runners_data.comment: Modest by bare results — nothing better than 4th in her last five starts, including a 7th last time out — but a strong speed figure hints at more; quick to return within 7 days and with proven distance/going form, she's open to outrunning that record here.

runners_data.name: Penny Mountain
runners_data.note: Jake Dickson (7lb claimer) rides for the in-form Gary Rutherford yard; Penny Mountain has been placed at 6f and 7f in recent outings in good and soft ground and brings consistent form to the table, but like several others in this field she is a hold-up type who cannot get her preferred rearward position in this particular race shape, which is her main tactical handicap.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent without threatening to win, with three 3rd-placed finishes among her last six starts and a 5th last time out; quick to return within 8 days and with proven distance/going form, but she looks held on these figures.

runners_data.name: Imperial Guard
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners the top weight (140lbs) for Michael Dods, and recent form reads poorly (9th, 6th, 8th) with all five of his last runs at 5f-6f on good ground — stepping up to 7f may help, but the form trajectory is heading the wrong way and there is nothing in his profile to suggest a sudden reversal of fortune here.|
runners_data.comment: Modest by bare results — nothing better than 5th in his last five starts — but he owns the strongest underlying figures here and returns quickly within 12 days; the yard's poor recent record is the concern, but on capability he's the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Jkr Cobbler
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 7f on good ground (1 in form string) and returns just eight days later for Iain Jardine, who is in outstanding form (9/32 T14); Jack Nicholls rides on a 5lb claim, and with a prominent style that allows him to slot in just off Ramon Di Loria, he is ideally suited to the likely race shape — his recent winning run and the trainer's current strike rate are both significant positives.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out for a yard in red-hot form (9 winners from 32 runners in the last fortnight), and he's quick to return within 8 days with proven distance/going form; the query is whether that upturn holds against these.

runners_data.name: War Memorial
runners_data.note: Conor Whiteley (5lb claimer) partners a horse with two wins from five runs at 7f on good ground and a second at the same trip, making him arguably the most proven hold-up closer in the field over this exact course configuration; the 21-day break is not a concern for Lawrence Mullaney's yard, and his profile is the most naturally suited of all the rear-runners to delivering a genuine late challenge if the pace holds.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, and that's the second win in his last six starts, though a 7th sits three starts back amid otherwise workmanlike form; a 21-day gap and modest speed figures leave questions, but proven distance/going form keeps him involved.

races.paceDynamic: Ramon Di Loria is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, crucially, faces no identified horse willing or able to pressure him from the outset on this flat 7f Ayr track in good ground. With Jkr Cobbler the only other prominent-style runner, the early fractions are likely to be controlled and sustainable, meaning Ramon Di Loria can dictate a measured gallop without expending unnecessary energy — a significant tactical advantage at this level. The pace map shows a cluster of hold-up types in the rear half of the field, but many of those — Monhammer, Penny Mountain, Bantz and Due Respect — are redistributed horses who cannot all settle naturally at the back as they would prefer, meaning the midfield will be congested and their finishing kicks may be blunted by positional friction. This race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently and travel well within themselves, with a controlled early pace setting up a stamina-testing finish where those who get a clean run from the front or just off it will be hardest to peg back; true hold-up closers face the double jeopardy of a slow gallop and a compressed midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria dictates a sustainable pace unchallenged and the race develops as a steadily-run affair.
scenarios.body: Ramon Di Loria sets a comfortable tempo, with Jkr Cobbler the only horse able to track him through the first half of the race, meaning the front pair enjoy a significant positional advantage entering the final 2f. Horses racing prominently conserve energy in the early stages and are best placed to quicken or grind out the finish on good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria and Jkr Cobbler go too hard early and the pace falls apart in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A slightly faster-than-expected opening splits the field, with the front two paying for it late, creating a genuine opportunity for horses that have tracked at the rear of a legitimate gallop to come through with a sustained run. War Memorial's proven form on this track and at this trip in good ground makes him the standout candidate to capitalise, with Imperial Guard's top weight suggesting class to close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Positional Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the congested midfield causes interference and one horse finds a clear passage to challenge late.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of Monhammer, Penny Mountain, Bantz and Due Respect into a compressed midfield creates a traffic-management problem, and the horse who gets a clean run on the outside early in the straight will benefit disproportionately from that positional chaos. Penny Mountain's consistent placed form at 6-7f in similar ground and the in-form Gary Rutherford yard make her the most interesting runner in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and one of the lower-weighted hold-up horses finds daylight from an unpredictable position.
scenarios.body: A messy race with multiple positional adjustments early could benefit a horse sitting just off the pace and switching off well, allowing it to produce a single sustained run through a gap. Bantz has the form figures buried within modest runs that suggest he can place if the conditions conspire, and Tap Dancer, stepping back sharply in trip from 10f+ campaigns, is an unknown quantity that could surprise if conditions suit.

watchPoints.text: Ramon Di Loria's ability to control the tempo without being pressed is the defining tactical factor — if he gets an uncontested lead at a fair pace, he becomes significantly harder to catch given the congested midfield behind him.

The midfield cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Monhammer, Penny Mountain, Bantz, Due Respect) creates a genuine traffic hazard entering the 2f pole — watch for horses getting hampered or stuck behind tiring rivals with nowhere to go.
Tap Dancer's trip drop from 10f-11f to 7f is completely uncharted — if he fails to settle in the first 3f, he could run well below expectations and also cause interference to horses around him.

Jkr Cobbler's trainer Iain Jardine is at 9/32 in the last 14 days and the horse won last time out over this exact trip and going — if connections have returned quickly with purpose, he is a major player in the prominent-run scenario.

War Memorial is the hold-up horse in this field with the strongest verified winning form at 7f on good going — track his early position closely, as any clear run he gets in the final 2f will make him the primary threat to the front-running pair.

races.name: Racing TV Handicap

runners_data.name: Pearl Eye
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old arrives on a 16-day turnaround with a recent win over 9f on good ground and strong similar-going form (1W3P from 12 runs), making her the most course-and-distance consistent closer in the field; her hold-up style means she depends on Spiritoftheblues not stealing a march, but Paul Mulrennan knows this horse well.
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back headlines a spell that also features two thirds, and he's quickly back here, just 16 days on, already proven over today's distance and going. That form and fitness make him the one to beat, with only a sixth last time out to note.

runners_data.name: Pol Roger
runners_data.note: Michael Dods sends out this six-year-old 24 days after his last run with a record of two placings at 10f on good ground but zero wins in similar conditions; Connor Beasley will need to deliver a career-best to trouble the front-runner from a hold-up position in a small field where there is little cover.
runners_data.comment: Pol Roger was third last time out, and a runner-up effort on his prior start gives him his two best of the spell; today's distance and going are proven. He stays without a win in the run, with a couple of below-par efforts further back the main query.

runners_data.name: Polygram
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's four-year-old has placed twice at distances of 11-12f on good ground and carries honest credentials at the trip, but his true racing style is closer to the back of the field than his mapped position suggests — he is a genuine hold-up type squeezed out of that role here; with a T14 of 1/11 and no win in six, the angles are modest.
runners_data.comment: Polygram was fourth last time out, backed up by a third on her prior start — the best of her recent form — and she has distance and going proven. Still without a win in that spell, and she has had over a month off since her last run.

runners_data.name: Spiritoftheblues
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old is the sole confirmed pace-setter, and with Daniel Tudhope in the saddle and a win over 7f on good ground among recent form, she is ideally placed to control this contest; the STYLE_FIT flag notes she may be racing slightly outside her optimal profile, but in a field of five with no rival to push her early, that risk is minimal.
runners_data.comment: Spiritoftheblues was runner-up last time out, and won earlier in this run, with a couple of below-par efforts in between; distance and going are proven. The one query is 26 days since that run, but she rates our second-best here.

runners_data.name: Light The Night Up
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's three-year-old arrives fresh off just a 10-day break with a string of placed efforts but no win from seven starts; she is a natural hold-up horse who cannot get to her preferred position here given the field composition, and her form has been exclusively on going softer than good, making the surface a secondary concern alongside the positional challenge.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts, with the form drifting the wrong way - two thirds further back fading to two fourths and a fifth last time out. Quick to return here, just 10 days on and with today's going proven, but this looks the outsider on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Spiritoftheblues is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no genuine rivals to push her early, she is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 1m2f trip on good ground at Ayr. With Pearl Eye, Pol Roger, Polygram, and Light The Night Up all operating from hold-up or midfield positions, Spiritoftheblues will lead unopposed and can dictate the fractions to suit her own stamina and finishing kick. The three hold-up types — Pearl Eye, Pol Roger, and the redistributed Polygram and Light The Night Up — will be chasing a pace-setter who is under no pressure, which risks the front-runner getting an uncontested lead and dictating a modest tempo that blunts late-running efforts. This race shape strongly favours the front-running/prominent profile: an uncontested leader on good ground over a middle-distance trip is the definition of a scenario where closers must cover ground and hope the pace has been genuine enough to reel the leader back in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Spiritoftheblues Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Spiritoftheblues leads without serious early pressure and controls the pace throughout.
scenarios.body: She sets a sustainable gallop, holds plenty in reserve turning for home, and makes the race a test of raw ability rather than stamina or tactical positioning; Daniel Tudhope can time his effort to perfection from the front. This shape suits front-runners and prominent racers most, and with no rival capable of matching her early, Spiritoftheblues is in an ideal tactical position despite the STYLE_FIT caveat on her OR figure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Spiritoftheblues sets a genuinely strong early pace that leaves her vulnerable in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected tempo would empty Spiritoftheblues out late, giving the hold-up horses — particularly Pearl Eye with her course-and-distance form and proven ability on good ground — a realistic target to chase down. Pearl Eye's record of a win at 9f on good and multiple placings in similar conditions makes her the most likely beneficiary of a pace collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Polygram Runs On Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to create a true-run race and Polygram finds a clear run from his natural hold-up position.
scenarios.body: Polygram has placed twice at distances beyond a mile on good ground and holds a live each-way profile if the tempo is genuinely searching; however, his redistribution out of his natural role and modest recent form (no win in six, rated 67) make this a low-probability outcome. His yard's T14 strike rate of 1/11 does little to boost confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Light The Night Up Improves
scenarios.trigger: If Light The Night Up, fresh off a 10-day turnaround, steps forward and the race develops to suit a horse finishing from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Trained by K. R. Burke and ridden by Pierre-Louis Jamin, Light The Night Up has shown consistent placing form (three thirds in recent runs) but has not yet won and has failed to place on going quicker than Standard; this scenario requires everything to fall right for a horse that has never won and is racing out of natural position. A six-runner field this small gives limited cover for a true hold-up horse needing traffic-free running late.

watchPoints.text: Watch Spiritoftheblues's early sectionals — if Tudhope pings the gates and sets a genuinely fast pace for a 1m2f race on good ground, the hold-up horses could be left with too much to do, gifting the race to the front-runner before the home turn.

Pearl Eye is the most likely closer to threaten if the pace softens — Paul Mulrennan may push her closer than her usual hold-up position to avoid being caught flat-footed in a small field with a solo leader.

Polygram and Light The Night Up are both true hold-up types forced into a midfield role by the field composition; watch whether either can find a clean run in the straight given the limited runners ahead of them may fan wide early.

With only five runners and a single pace-setter, the field is likely to bunch through the early stages — jockeys on hold-up types may choose to sit closer than usual, effectively compressing the field and making the race more of a one-pace affair that blunts the advantage of a late-running style.

races.name: Every Race Live On Racing TV Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Inappropriate
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer who has shown ability at similar trips on Good ground — two places from two comparable runs — with headgear (tp) to assist concentration; 19 days since last run is a straightforward return, but as a genuine closer this shape does not ideally suit.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and twice a runner-up in its last five starts, form that already includes today's going and a prompt reappearance just 19 days on. Still without a win in that spell, but the profile and fitness edge make it our narrow preference here.

runners_data.name: Simply Ruby
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old is the sole confirmed front runner and shapes as a key race-organiser; a long 292-day absence is a significant unknown, her OR=74 is the highest in the field, and if fitness holds she controls this race from the front — though racing out of role in any shape that requires following is a concern (STYLE_FIT=0.90).
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back stands out in her recent form, and she already has today's distance and going covered, from a yard currently in good form. The concern is fitness following a seventh last time out and the best part of ten months off the track.

runners_data.name: Simple Star
runners_data.note: Dianne Sayer's eight-year-old has the most relevant Going and trip profile of any runner — 12 Good-ground runs producing two wins and five places — and Molly Gunn's claim is an asset at the weights; a hold-up style means she is reliant on others setting a testing gallop, which this race may not produce.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and again five starts back, bookending a tougher middle stretch of the sequence, and already proven over today's distance and going. Still without a win in that run, but our figure sits above the official mark.

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's seven-year-old has won twice at 15-16f on Good ground in his last five starts and carries genuine form credentials; a true hold-up horse whose deep closing style has been mapped to midfield due to field congestion, so his chance is somewhat contingent on the race developing more pace than Simply Ruby is likely to create.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in its last five starts - three and five starts back - show solid recent form, and he's already proven over today's distance and going. Quickly back out again just nine days on from a fourth last time out, his only finish outside the top three in that run.

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: Oliver Carmichael rides Goldie's second string, a prominent racer with two wins from five Good-ground runs and a recent run just seven days ago suggesting peak fitness; ideally drawn in terms of race shape — able to track the leader and kick on without needing a searing gallop to be involved.
runners_data.comment: One win in its last six starts, followed by two thirds including last time out, with mixed form earlier in the sequence. Only a week since its latest run and already suited by today's distance and going, but rated the outsider on our figures.

runners_data.name: Glasses Up
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old with a losing run stretching back through his last six starts and the lowest OR in the race at 54; a natural hold-up type placed at midfield due to field distribution, and his recent form over shorter trips (9-10f) at lower OR levels is a further concern at this trip and in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in its last six starts, with a best effort of third five starts back among mostly modest finishes. Proven over today's distance and going, and our figure sits above the official mark, but the recent form reads on the poor side.

races.paceDynamic: Simply Ruby is the lone confirmed front runner in this six-runner field over 1m5f on Good ground at Ayr, and with no genuine rival willing to press her for the lead, she is likely to control the gallop at a sustainable, even tempo. Behind her, Annandale figures to track prominently in second or third, while Inappropriate, Cascade Hall, and Glasses Up are true hold-up types who will settle towards the rear — though Cascade Hall and Glasses Up, despite being natural closers, have been redistributed to midfield in the map because the rear of the field is more congested with hold-up horses than the visual layout can accommodate. With Simply Ruby dictating an unchallenged, measured pace, the race is unlikely to develop the searching gallop that would stretch a free-finishing closer — instead this shape systematically advantages horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort through the final quarter-mile without needing a pronounced late surge. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can sit close to the controlled pace and grind past a front runner in the straight are best positioned, while pure hold-up horses dependent on a true end-to-end gallop to generate their finish are structurally disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Simply Ruby Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Simply Ruby is allowed to dictate a calm, uncontested pace throughout and the hold-up horses cannot generate sufficient momentum from the rear.
scenarios.body: Simply Ruby sets her own fractions with Lewis Chalkley able to conserve energy through the middle stages, arriving at the home straight with reserves intact while closers lack the required gap to bridge; Annandale, sitting just behind, is ideally placed to chase her down if she tires, making Jim Goldie's prominent runners the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Annandale tracks Simply Ruby at close quarters and the two prominent types exhaust the field, reducing the race to a sustained war of attrition in the straight.
scenarios.body: Oliver Carmichael on Annandale can use fresh legs after only seven days since last run, sitting a length or two off the leader and accelerating past in the final furlong on the flat Ayr straight; Simple Star, who shows solid Good-ground form over this trip with two wins and five places in 15 similar-going runs, may stay on for a place.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Simply Ruby's unchallenged lead creates a false pace that collapses in the straight, opening the door for hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Cascade Hall brings strong credentials — two wins from six Good-ground runs including a win at 15f — and if Annandale or Simply Ruby set a pace that ultimately proves too fast for the flat finish, Jake Dickson can deliver a strong late run; however, this scenario is structurally discounted because both Cascade Hall and Glasses Up are redistributed from their natural rear position and may not achieve ideal separation to launch a true finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Rank Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If Simply Ruby is pulled up or loses her lead early, creating a disorganised race with no true pace and a messy finish.
scenarios.body: Without a leader to organise the race, the field bunches and the outcome becomes unpredictable, potentially favouring a fresh-legged horse who happens to be best positioned in the straight; Glasses Up, an 11-year-old with declining form and the lowest OR in the field, represents only a token threat even in this chaotic shape.

watchPoints.text: Simply Ruby's 292-day absence is the single biggest race-shape threat — if she returns short of fitness and fades from the front, the entire dominant scenario unravels and Annandale becomes the primary beneficiary.

Cascade Hall and Glasses Up are both genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield due to redistribution — watch how Jake Dickson and Shay Farmer actually position them from the gates, as achieving true rear-of-field positions would change the dynamic for the closers' scenarios.

Annandale ran only seven days ago and Jim Goldie's 14-day record is 6 wins from 46 runners — watch whether Oliver Carmichael is instructed to race conservatively early or to push up aggressively behind Simply Ruby, which will determine whether this turns into a two-horse race.

Simple Star's trainer Dianne Sayer has a 2/3 record over the past 14 days — a small but sharp strike rate — and the mare's Good-ground record at this trip makes her a legitimate place contender if the pace is even moderate.
